title: dumpcap: Ensure the buffer size is large enough for the SHB
description:
A SHB can have comments and other options, so it is possible (if a
bit odd) to have a length larger than the initial 2048 size buffer.
Move the "round up a 32 bit integer to the next highest power of 2"
function to a static function.

Check if the SHB block size is less than the minimum.

Move a block size is a multiple of 4 check for a SHB until after
the endianness is determined.

Add some comments. There probably should be an imposed maximum
(but see commit db9ed8844c48326a3a8e3823d1d9f152e6667542).

Fix #21132

AI-Assisted: no

notes.body: enabled automatic add to merge train when checks pass
Hey, why not? Dunno if anybody *else* is doing this, but maybe somebody will want to do so at some point.

If we're contemplating a utility function for this, I'd suggest we make use of the bit-manipulation intrinsics supported by both [GCC](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Bit-Operation-Builtins.html) and [Clang](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/LanguageExtensions.html#intrinsics-support-within-constant-expressions) in preference to the bit-hack.  Those intrinsics will often compile to a single instruction utilising CPU hardware to extract the index of the most-significant '1' bit.  The bit-hack can stay as a fallback in case we encounter a compiler without support for those intrinsics.
